title: Christmas Silver Coins: 2026 Releases and What to Check
summary: The 2026 Christmas silver coins from the Perth Mint and others, how to tell a legal tender coin from a Santa round, and what to check before you wrap one.
body_markdown:
The Perth Mint's 2026 Christmas coin is out, and it's about as clear an example of the genre as you'll find: two ounces of 99.99% silver, a colored village of gingerbread houses on the reverse, a little enameled gingerbread man set into the middle, and a $2 face value as[Australian legal tender](https://www.perthmint.com/shop/collector-coins/coins/gingerbread-christmas-2026-2oz-silver-antiqued-coloured-coin/) . That is a Christmas silver coin in the strict sense. A lot of what turns up under the same search is something else. Usually that means a privately made silver round with Santa on it. A perfectly nice present, but not a coin, and if the label on the box is part of the gift you'll want to know which one you're holding.


We run Pure, a marketplace for coins and bullion. The festive pieces below link to the mints that make them, and Pure only shows up at the end, for plain silver.


## What the mints have released for Christmas 2026


Checked October 8, 2026. Mints keep adding holiday pieces into November, so this list will grow.


### Perth Mint: Gingerbread Christmas 2026


Perth does one of these every year now. Last year's was[Santa's Workshop](https://www.perthmint.com/shop/collector-coins/coins/santas-workshop-2025-2oz-silver-antiqued-coloured-coin/) , also 2 oz, antiqued and colored.


This year it's gingerbread people carolling, sledding and building snowmen, with King Charles III on the obverse in the Dan Thorne effigy. The antiquing is done coin by coin, and the mint says the finish may vary across the mintage. The one you get may not match the photo exactly. It comes in a clear-lidded display case inside a white box tied with a ribbon, with a numbered certificate of authenticity.


It's a decoration made of silver. If that's what you're after, start here.


### Royal Canadian Mint: holiday coins, just not silver ones


The Royal Canadian Mint's[holiday gifts page](https://www.mint.ca/en/shop/gifts/holiday) has two 2026 pieces, both base metal. The[Whimsical Winter lenticular coin](https://www.mint.ca/en/shop/coins/2026/whimsical-winter-lenticular-coin-2026) is a nickel-plated steel 50 cents, 12.3 g, with a picture that flips from a winter day to a snowy night when you tilt it. The[Holiday Gift Card Set](https://www.mint.ca/en/shop/coins/2026/holiday-gift-card-set-2026-pack-252758) is five uncirculated coins in a greeting card, including a set-only $1 of Canada geese in toques singing carols under a street lamp.


Good stocking fillers, and both ship to the US. Neither is silver.


The one silver Christmas coin on that page is dated 2025, and it ships within Canada only.


### The Royal Mint: The Snowman 50p


Britain's Christmas coin is a 50p with Raymond Briggs' Snowman on it. The 2025 design, the Snowman and James stringing lights on a tree, was the eighth since the character first appeared on UK coins in 2018, and the Royal Mint offered it in several finishes, none of them released into circulation ([Coin World](https://www.coinworld.com/news/world-coins/royal-mint-revives-the-snowman-holiday-treat-with-a-twist) ). The version tucked into that year's advent calendar was a colorized Brilliant Uncirculated coin. That write-up doesn't give the metal for each finish, so read the spec line if silver is the point.


No 2026 Snowman had been announced when we looked. The 2025 release was pitched as a first coin for kids.


### Coins struck for small countries


That 2025 silver piece on the Canadian site is a good illustration of how a lot of themed coins get made. The Snowman Winter Sleigh Ride is[legal tender of the Solomon Islands](https://www.mint.ca/en/shop/coins/2025/snowman-winter-sleigh-ride-fine-silver-coin) , $2 face value, 31.39 g of 99.99% silver, made by MKS PAMP for an American company and sold through the Royal Canadian Mint's shop.


That's normal. The American Numismatic Association calls these[non-circulating legal tender](https://blog.money.org/coin-collecting/circulating-and-non-circulating-legal-tender) : a sovereign nation issues them with a denomination, private mints make them under contract, and technically they are money, though nobody spends them.


### Private-mint Christmas rounds


Santas, sleighs, snowmen, nativity scenes. They fill most of Google's shopping results for this search, and they're rounds. A round is struck by a private company with no face value and no issuing country. Asked about one by a reader,[Coin World](https://www.coinworld.com/news/world-coins/privately-minted-silver-round.html) put it flatly: it is not legal tender, and an ounce of .999 silver is valued off the spot price of silver.


For a present that's fine, as long as the listing says round.


## How to tell a coin from a round from a token


Ignore the product title. The spec block settles it, and three lines do most of the work:


-


**Face value.** A coin has one ($2, 50 cents, $1). A round has none, and won't pretend to.


-


**Country of issue.** Perth writes "Australian legal tender" on the page; the Royal Canadian Mint lists "Country of issue" on coins it sells for other countries.


-


**Composition.** "Fine silver" with a fineness number. Steel, brass or "silver plated" means it's a souvenir, whatever the title says.


A few of the "Christmas coins" in the shopping results for this search say gold plated or silver plated right in the title. Plenty of others don't say anything.


## What to check before you wrap one


**Fineness.** Perth's Christmas coins are .9999 and the Silver Eagle is .999. A lower number means an alloy. The .958 in[Britannia silver](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-is-britannia-silver) is still silver, just not fine silver.


**Weight.** Coin weights are troy ounces, heavier than the ounce on a kitchen scale (the[troy ounce](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-is-a-troy-ounce) explainer has the conversion). Two troy ounces is about 62 grams. On a colored coin with an insert, look for the stated silver content as well as the gross weight.


**Packaging.** Leave it sealed. The Solomon Islands sleigh coin ships in a capsule built to hang on a tree. Charming, and it also keeps fingers off the surface. Handled silver tones.


**Certificate versus grade.** A numbered certificate of authenticity is the mint's own paper saying what it made. A grade is a third party's opinion of condition on the[1 to 70 Sheldon scale](https://www.ngccoin.com/coin-grading/grading-scale/) , sealed in a plastic slab. The mint releases above ship with the first, not the second.


**Time.** If it's going under a tree, order early enough that delivery isn't the thing you're waiting on.


## Silver under the tree, minus the Santa


Most of the Silver Eagles you see sold in Christmas cards and holiday tins are ordinary Silver Eagles. The law fixes that coin at[40.6 mm, 31.103 grams, .999 fine silver](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/31/5112) , with Liberty on one side and an eagle on the other, so the festive part is the card or tin a seller wraps around it.


That's the honest case for skipping the theme. A plain[2026 Silver Eagle](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/2026-american-silver-eagle-1-oz-999-fine-1-coin-0217) or a[random-date one](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/american-silver-eagle-1-oz-varied-year000225) is a full troy ounce of silver from the US Mint, and you can put your own card on it. On Pure, we test every item ourselves before it ships, items that pass ship Pure Qualified, and shipping is insured. Prices are sellers' asks quoted against live spot, so the[silver chart](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/silver) tells you where the metal sits that day.


[Gold and silver gifts on Pure](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/gold-silver-gifts) collects what's listed at gift-sized prices, and our[gold and silver gift ideas](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/gold-and-silver-gift-ideas) cover the rest of the options. If the person already stacks silver,[gifts for silver collectors](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/gifts-for-silver-collectors) is the list for them.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much is a silver Christmas coin worth?


Two different numbers. One is the silver inside it, which is arithmetic: weight times fineness times the day's silver price. The other is the price itself, which also covers the design, the color and the box. Put a 2 oz collector coin's price next to two ounces on the[silver chart](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/silver) and the gap is what you're paying for the gift part. For a round,[Coin World's answer](https://www.coinworld.com/news/world-coins/privately-minted-silver-round.html) was simpler: its value is based on the spot price of silver.


### What coin goes in a Christmas pudding?


A silver sixpence. It's a British custom the[Royal Mint traces to the Victorian era](https://www.royalmint.com/stories/gifts/stir-up-sunday-and-the-christmas-sixpence/) : the family stirs the pudding on Stir-up Sunday, the Sunday before Advent, everyone makes a wish, the coin goes in, and whoever finds it on Christmas Day gets the luck for the year. In 2026 Stir-up Sunday is November 22. Tell people before they bite.


### Is a colored silver coin still real silver?


Yes, if the spec says so. The Perth and Royal Canadian Mint pages both list their colored Christmas coins as 99.99% silver, the Canadian page literally as "99.99% pure silver with colour." The color is part of the design, and the silver content on the spec line is the same either way.
